questions.prompt: What is the safest way to use a type or build feature?
options: Assume compiler configuration has identical behavior in every version.
Use any whenever the types become difficult.
Treat type-level examples as proof of runtime correctness.
Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
questions.answer_key: Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
questions.explanation: Type and build features must be evaluated in the actual configured project.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Typed Arrays”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with array type syntax and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with array type syntax and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Array type syntax”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Typed Arrays”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check arrays of objects, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume readonly arrays is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check arrays of objects, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Arrays of objects”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
